title: GST Registration, Persons Liable and Cancellation

content.overview: A person must register if aggregate turnover exceeds the threshold, or if the Act requires registration regardless of turnover, including inter-State suppliers in the cases enacted, casual and non-resident taxable persons, and persons required to pay tax on reverse charge where the section so requires. Registration can be cancelled for the stated defaults. A person below the threshold may register voluntarily. Liability to register is not the same as liability on one invoice. Threshold and compulsory classes are different gates.
content.glance: GST Registration, Persons Liable and Cancellation. Complete Tax treatise with statutory deconstruction, examples, verified authorities, forum analysis and chamber drafting.
content.study: Compute turnover only to identify the gate. Then check the compulsory list before saying registration is optional.

cases.name: Govind Saran Ganga Saran v. Commissioner of Sales Tax
cases.facts: The Court examined the components of a valid charging provision.
cases.issue: What must a tax levy clearly identify to be valid?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A valid levy ordinarily identifies the taxable event, person liable, rate and measure or value of the tax.
cases.holding: The Court treated these components as essential to a charging scheme.

cases.name: Union of India v. Azadi Bachao Andolan
cases.facts: The Court considered treaty benefits, circulars and tax avoidance arguments.
cases.issue: How should a valid tax treaty and administrative circular operate?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A treaty and valid administrative practice must be respected unless displaced by law; legitimate tax planning is not automatically evasion.
cases.holding: The Court upheld the challenged treaty approach in the circumstances.
cases.relevance: Use for statutory interpretation, treaties and tax planning.

cases.name: Union of India v. Mohit Minerals Pvt. Ltd.
cases.facts: The case concerned GST levy and the legal effect of a Council recommendation.
cases.issue: What is the constitutional and statutory force of GST Council recommendations?
cases.ratioDecidendi: GST Council recommendations have persuasive value within the constitutional design but are not automatically binding as primary legislation without statutory implementation.
cases.holding: The Court interpreted the federal GST framework accordingly.
cases.relevance: Use for GST levy, delegated action and constitutional federalism.

enhancement.definition: A person must register if aggregate turnover exceeds the threshold, or if the Act requires registration regardless of turnover, including inter-State suppliers in the cases enacted, casual and non-resident taxable persons, and persons required to pay tax on reverse charge where the section so requires. Registration can be cancelled for the stated defaults. A person below the threshold may register voluntarily.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Liability to register is not the same as liability on one invoice. Threshold and compulsory classes are different gates.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 22 is the threshold. Section 24 lists persons who must register irrespective of turnover. The exact threshold and special-category figure are notifications and are not frozen here. Distinct persons in each State register separately where the Act requires it. Cancellation under section 29 includes contravention, non-filing and discontinuance, with a chance to be heard where the section requires it.
examples: A trader crosses the threshold in one State.
A person in the compulsory list registers even below the threshold.
A registered person stops business and applies for cancellation.
enhancement.problemApplication: Compute turnover only to identify the gate. Then check the compulsory list before saying registration is optional.
enhancement.caseLawNotes: No new case citation or ratio was added. Rates and notifications are not frozen in this note.
